body:
Marissa Cole: Question for the group: should we add an “Email preferences” link directly in Console Settings (e.g., Settings → Notifications) as part of the lifecycle sprint? Right now it’s only in the emails themselves.

Paula Mendes: From telemetry POV, I like it. Support keeps getting “I didn’t get the email / how do I unsubscribe” and it’s awkward to tell them to find a footer link in an email they didn’t receive.

Ben Carter: +1. Also reduces risk w/ CAN-SPAM complaints if people can quickly opt out. But we need to be clear what we’re letting them control: onboarding lifecycle vs product/security.

Tyler Benson: Marketing ops angle: having a consistent preference center helps deliverability. If users can’t find unsub easily, they hit “Report spam” and that burns our domain.

Dylan Brooks: Implementation-wise, are we thinking a deep link to the existing preferences page (hosted somewhere) or a native settings page?

Marissa Cole: Ideally a simple native page in-console (same auth), but a link is fine if it’s behind auth + correct user context.

Ethan Park: If we do a link, we need an endpoint that can render when logged in, not the “one-click” unsub token link. The token link is email-specific and should still work if you’re logged out.

Michael Grant: Legal/compliance: having an in-app preferences surface is generally good. Two big cautions:
1) Don’t make it confusing: users must be able to opt out of marketing/lifecycle emails without accidentally opting out of transactional (billing, security, outage).
2) GDPR: if we call it “preferences,” ensure we’re honoring the choice quickly and logging consent state changes.

Olga Petrov: +1 to Michael. Also for EU users: if we’re using behavior-based segmentation (“stalled user”), make sure the preference center explains categories at a high level. We don’t need to list every trigger, but should not be misleading.

Kenji Nakamura: UX question: where exactly in Settings? We already have “Account,” “API Keys,” “Billing.” Adding “Notifications” might be the right grouping, but we should keep it simple. Could also be a single line under Account: “Manage email preferences.”

Marissa Cole: I’m leaning “Account → Emails” with a small description: “Control onboarding and product updates. Critical account emails can’t be disabled.”

Ben Carter: Re: wording, please avoid “product updates” if that’s marketing-y. Our lifecycle drip is mostly onboarding help. Maybe “Onboarding tips and announcements”? (Soojin had strong opinions last week :slightly_smiling_face:)

Tyler Benson: We should also add a link to the prefs page from the console header help menu? Folks look there when they’re stuck. But that might be scope creep.

Dylan Brooks: Tech/eng: if we build a native prefs page, we need to define what preferences we store. My proposal:
- `onboarding_emails_enabled` (default true)
- `product_marketing_enabled` (default true)
- `sales_outreach_enabled` (default true?) TBD
And we explicitly *exclude* transactional from this system.

Paula Mendes: For measurement: we should emit an event when someone changes preferences so we can monitor if the new email sequence is causing opt-outs to spike.

Michael Grant: Please be careful with “sales_outreach_enabled” as a toggle. Depending on jurisdiction, sales emails may fall under different rules. Also, if Sales is using separate tooling/CRM sequences, we might not be able to fully honor it unless we wire it end-to-end.

Olga Petrov: Agree. If we can’t guarantee it across all systems, don’t expose the toggle yet. Start with lifecycle/onboarding only (since that’s the sprint).

Ben Carter: +1. Scope it to onboarding/lifecycle emails for now. Anything sales-related should go through the existing CRM preferences / opt-out handling.

Ethan Park: Implementation detail: we need to ensure the lifecycle sender checks the preference at send time (not only at cohort assignment). Otherwise a user can opt out and still get the next scheduled send.

Dylan Brooks: Yup. Also need to update suppression logic for “unsubscribe all” and store it centrally. (We already have a few scattered checks in the send pipeline.)

Marissa Cole: OK, decision proposal:
- Add a “Manage email preferences” link in Console Settings (Account).
- First version controls only onboarding/lifecycle emails.
- Copy clearly states: “You’ll still receive critical account emails (billing/security).”
- Emit `email_preferences_updated` event.
Michael/Olga can you review copy + categories?

Michael Grant: Works for me. Send me the draft strings; I’ll sanity check for CAN-SPAM language + clarity.

Olga Petrov: Same. Also include locale handling plan (even if it’s English-only now, avoid idioms).

Tyler Benson: I’ll add a quick checklist for marketing ops: ensure the preference state is reflected in SendGrid suppressions + internal segment logic. Also please don’t forget the footer link still needs to remain in every message.

Dylan Brooks: I’ll create an eng task for the settings link + page route behind auth. We can gate behind the lifecycle sprint feature flag and roll out gradually.

Marissa Cole: Great. I’ll update the sprint notes + ping @Ben Carter when we have the first build ready for QA.
